STEP 1 - Scene: The meal is two short pieces of corn on the cob, cut into rounds and viewed end-on, on a square white plate.

STEP 2 - Vessel: The plate is square, about 24 cm across. Treated as roughly a 26 cm dinner plate, the area is about 3.14 × 13² ≈ 530 cm².

STEP 3 - Items: The only food is two corn cob rounds. I see no butter or sauce.

STEP 4 - Area: Each round is about 7 cm in diameter, so it covers about 38 cm². That is roughly 7% of the plate, or about 14% for both together.

STEP 5 - Volume: Each piece looks about 4 cm tall. That gives 38 cm² × 4 cm ≈ 154 ml per piece, or about 308 ml in total.

STEP 6 - Grams: Corn on the cob, including the cob, is fairly dense at about 0.7 g/ml. That gives 308 × 0.7 ≈ 215 g gross. The cob makes up about 40% of that and is inedible, so the edible kernels come to about 130 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Boiled corn kernels have about 96 kcal per 100 g. So 130 g × 0.96 ≈ 125 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Two half-ears of corn giving about 130 g of kernels and about 125 kcal is plausible.
